statement: Dimensional weight is length x width x height divided by 5000 and rounded up to the next whole gram, so 101 x 101 x 101 gives 207 g.

faults.description: Rounds the dimensional weight down instead of up, so 101 x 101 x 101 gives 206 g instead of 207 g.
Uses width twice and ignores height in the volume, so 300 x 200 x 100 gives 2400 g instead of 1200 g.

statement: The standard rate is 450 cents for the first 500 g step plus the zone's per-extra-step charge for each further step, so 1500 g in zone 3 costs 730 cents.

faults.description: Charges the per-step rate for every step, including the first, so 1500 g in zone 3 costs 870 cents instead of 730.
Changes the zone 3 per-extra-step charge from 140 to 150 cents, so 1500 g in zone 3 costs 750 cents instead of 730.

statement: Express costs the standard base times 1.75 rounded half up to the cent plus 300 cents, and billable weight above 20000 g is rejected for express with ExpressWeightLimit.

faults.description: Drops the half-up rounding step, so a standard base of 730 cents gives 1277 + 300 = 1577 instead of 1578.
Forces the express weight guard to never fire, so a 25000 g express parcel is priced instead of raising ExpressWeightLimit.

statement: Codes beginning with 99 or from 80000 to 80499 inclusive are remote and add 275 cents on standard and 400 cents on express, and a postal code that is not exactly five digits is rejected with InvalidPostalCode.

faults.description: Shrinks the remote range to end at 80400, so code 80450 is wrongly treated as non-remote.
Charges the standard 275-cent remote surcharge on express as well, so a remote express parcel is charged 275 instead of 400.

statement: The oversize surcharge is decided by the longest side alone: 500 cents from 600 to 999 mm, 1500 cents from 1000 mm, nothing below 600 mm, and only one charge ever applies.

faults.description: Takes the length as the longest side, so a parcel with width 1100 and length 100 is not charged for being oversize.
Charges the giant class on top of the large class (2000 cents), so a longest side of 1000 mm costs 2000 instead of 1500.

statement: quote returns an itemized breakdown of base, remote, oversize and total in cents, where total is base plus remote plus oversize, so a standard zone 2 1000 g parcel to 99120 with a 650 mm longest side totals 1315 cents.

faults.description: Passes the service and postal code to remote_surcharge in the wrong order, so quote raises InvalidPostalCode for an ordinary parcel.
Leaves the oversize surcharge out of the total without raising, so the 650 mm example totals 815 instead of 1315.
Reports the remote surcharge under the oversize item, so the breakdown shows oversize 275 instead of 500.

statement: tracking_number returns the prefix BP, the nine-digit zero-padded sequence and one check digit computed modulo 10, and rejects a sequence below 0 or above 999999999 with InvalidSequence.

faults.description: Lowers the accepted maximum to 99999999, so sequence 500000000 is wrongly rejected with InvalidSequence.
Omits the check digit from the returned tracking number, so only BP and nine digits are returned.
Leaves the check digit computation as a dangling modulo operator, which is a syntax error.
